text:
Sanjay: heads-up — saw a 2.3x jump in A100 spot interruptions in us-west1 this morning. I think our fixed-slab bidding is getting clipped. proposing a probabilistic hedging approach instead of a single mix ratio.
Anna: curious, what do you mean by probabilistic hedging here? quick summary pls.
Sanjay: instead of a static allocation (e.g. 70% price-opt / 30% capacity-opt), compute weights from recent interruption hazard and price dispersion. treat pools as random draws and hedge to keep expected interruption probability under a risk budget.
Mike: sounds interesting. how would we estimate the hazard? historical preemption rate over last N hours? any latency signals?
Sanjay: baseline idea: estimate r_region_gpu = exponential-smoothed preempt rate for (region,gpu_type). compute price_sigma = stddev of spot price / mean over window. then set pool_weight_i proportional to 1/(r_i * f(price_sigma)) with a floor so we still capture price wins.
Jessie: can you sketch config we'd push? would like something I can turn into our allocator rollout.
Sanjay: crude example config (for discussion):
```
{
  "pools": [
    {"id":"price_opt", "base_weight":0.6},
    {"id":"capacity_opt", "base_weight":0.3},
    {"id":"reserved_fallback", "base_weight":0.1}
  ],
  "bid_ceiling_pct": 12,      // max % above on-demand
  "risk_budget": 0.08,       // target expected interruption prob
  "warm_buffer": 4,
  "recompute_window_mins": 30
}
```
Anna: nice. what's the mapping from observed r -> weight? a short formula would help.
Sanjay: simplest: w_i = clamp( base_i * (1 / (1 + alpha * r_i)), min_w, max_w ) then normalize. alpha controls sensitivity. alpha tuned so a doubling in r halves weight contribution roughly.
Olivia: how do we handle cold starts when a region goes to zero capacity? fallback to reserved_fallback pool? and eviction churn will spike coldstarts.
Jessie: yes. operator flow: add soft-fallback route to dedicated reserved pool with instance startup probes. pre-warm N nodes in reserved_fallback per region to reduce coldstart latency. warm_buffer param controls that.
Mike: rollout plan idea: start with 5% of allocation under probabilistic hedging for one ASG in us-west1, monitor 1h for interruptions, tail latency, and unit cost. if stable, increment to 25%.
InfraBot: alert: spot-interrupt-rate(us-west1,A100) = 0.22 (2.2x baseline) — triggered at 1999876600
Sanjay: thanks infra-bot. also add change to our autoscaler: when interruption rate > threshold, temporarily increase reserved_fallback weight by delta_w for 15m to absorb churn.
Anna: good. also surface a runbook metric: "expected_interruption" = sum_i(w_i * r_i) and show both expected and realized. that gives us a single dial.
Jessie: I'll add a canary playbook: config, prom queries, alert thresholds, and a k8s job to apply the weights. will post PR with config snippets.
Mike: also add cost vs reliability chart: expected cost delta vs interruption reduction for alpha sweep. helps product decide risk_budget.
Sanjay: exactly. final note — document assumptions in PR: smoothing window, alpha, min_w, warm buffer cost. will iterate after initial canary.
Olivia: +1. please include region fallback ordering and a cap on cross-region spill (we don't want to move all workloads off eu-west1 into us-west1).
Sanjay: agreed — include max_cross_region_spill_pct = 0.2 in config.
Anna: awesome. assign the PR to Jessie and Sanjay, and tag oncall for the canary window. :thumbsup:
